html:
The Honduran coup of 2009 removed President Manuel Zelaya on 28 June 2009, when soldiers seized him at dawn and flew him to Costa Rica in his pajamas.

Zelaya, elected as a Liberal, had moved to the left and planned a poll on rewriting the constitution, which the courts and Congress said was illegal. The army acted on a court order to arrest him, but sent him abroad instead. Congress named its speaker, Roberto Micheletti, as president.

Most of the world condemned the coup, and Honduras was suspended from the Organization of American States. New elections that November brought in the National Party, which held power until 2022, when Zelaya's wife Xiomara Castro won the presidency. The years after were marked by violence, drug trafficking and migration, and by the memory of the Cold War coups of the region.
sum: The Honduran coup of 2009 removed President Manuel Zelaya on 28 June 2009, when soldiers seized him at dawn and flew him to Costa Rica in his pajamas.
